summary: Full backend + frontend testing of CorpScore KYB. Backend pytest: 15/16 passed (1 pytest-xdist test-scoping artifact, not a real bug). Frontend Playwright: owner login, applicant register, 4-step onboarding wizard, submit with screening + AI scoring, HIGH risk with 3 screening hits (Ali Rahman SANCTION + Budi Hartono Santoso PEP + self-declared PEP), applicant RBAC (no approve button), owner reject flow, logout, and Google button redirect all working end-to-end.

minor.issue: test_stats_applicant_scope fails under pytest-xdist parallel workers because module-scoped `applicant` fixture is re-instantiated on each worker; the applicant that ran TestDashboard didn't create apps. Backend behavior is correct — merely a test-design issue with xdist LoadScopeScheduling. Fix: move fixture to session scope or run without -n auto.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py `screen_watchlist` includes self-declared PEP but also duplicates when a watchlist PEP match exists on the same person — dedupe key is (matched_name, list) so both records (Self-declared PEP + Domestic PEP list) coexist; acceptable but produces the appearance of two PEP hits for one person.

compute_rule_score computes screening = 100 - 60*sanctions - 25*adverse - 15*peps: with only 1 SANCTION + 2 PEP hits this yields 100-60-30=10 which correctly drives HIGH; no issue but no floor per hit-type documented.
AI gpt-5.4 model string is unusual — main agent confirmed working; keep as-is.
set_auth_cookie uses samesite=none + secure=true which is required for cross-site cookie in preview; frontend also uses withCredentials + Bearer token from response body as fallback, both work.

download_document endpoint accepts `authorization`/`auth` params but does not actually validate user access — anyone with app_id+doc_id can download. Consider requiring auth and checking ownership/officer role.

rca of the issue: test_stats_applicant_scope failure RCA: pytest-xdist LoadScopeScheduling assigns TestDashboard to worker gw1 while TestApplication (which populates apps via the same-named `applicant` fixture) ran on gw0. Because the fixture is scope=module, each worker gets its own fresh applicant with 0 apps → assertion total>=2 fails on gw1. Mitigation: run `pytest --dist loadfile` or `pytest -p no:xdist`, or change fixture to session scope with shared state. Backend endpoint /api/dashboard/stats itself is correct.
